# Spec: merge-forward
<!-- Generated by /hefesto:hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-09 -->
<!-- Board item: HEF-31 -->

## Overview

A pull request whose base moved under it (GitHub `mergeStateStatus` `DIRTY` — conflicting — or `BEHIND`) is
today blocked `conflict`, and the orchestrator's **Retry** sends it back to the same babysitter, which blocks it
again (measured 2026-11-09 on PR #192). This feature makes the conflict a **build-stage job**: the entry moves
from `pr` back to `implement` with a helper-generated *merge-forward brief*; the implement worker merges the base
into the PR branch, resolves only what is mechanical, runs the project's tests, pushes to the same branch, and
the verifier re-runs its gates on the new head. A two-sided edit made with intent stops as a `human:clarify`
question carrying both hunks — never a guess.

## Context (as the code stands, cited)

- `hooks/pr-watch.sh:280-288` — verdict: `DIRTY` → `conflict`; `CLEAN|BEHIND|HAS_HOOKS` → `mergeable`.
- `commands/hef.babysit.md:138` — `conflict` → `ledger.sh block <id> --kind conflict` ("a rebase is not a babysitter fix").
- `hooks/session-launch.sh:428` — the headless deploy run's verdict `conflict` → block `conflict`.
- `hooks/ledger-recipes.sh:207-242` — the lane merge's state step routes `conflict|behind` to `merge_block_conflict`
  (phase stays `pr`); `action stop --block conflict` does the same.
- `commands/hef.orchestrate.md:161` — **Retry** on `conflict` → `ledger.sh unblock` → the entry, still in `pr`,
  goes back to the deploy pass's babysit: the loop.
- `hooks/ledger.sh:493-529` — `advance` moves forward only; `hooks/ledger-lifecycle.sh:133-157` — `reopen` is the
  only backward move, person-only, `merged` entries only. Its follow-up file (hashed, handed to the implement
  launch as data, `session-launch.sh:463`) is the precedent this feature copies.
- `hooks/ledger.sh:887-912` — `next --stage build` takes `implement` entries that are unowned and unblocked.
- `hooks/ledger-notes.sh:13-30` — a lane *directive* reaches the build lane, never the worker it launches
  (`ledger-lifecycle.sh:146-148`, live check 2026-10-29). So the brief is NOT a `ledger.sh directive`.

## Decisions (made from the code; no open question needed)

- **D1 — `BEHIND` needs no branch-protection read.** GitHub reports `mergeStateStatus: BEHIND` only when branch
  protection requires branches to be up to date before merging; without that rule a behind PR reads `CLEAN`. So
  "BEHIND with required up-to-date branches" is exactly `BEHIND`; no helper calls the protection API.
- **D2 — `pr-watch.sh state` gains a `behind` verdict** for `BEHIND` (no longer folded into `mergeable`).
  `ledger-recipes.sh` already maps `BEHIND` to `behind` for the lane merge; this makes the babysitter agree.
- **D3 — a new helper move, `ledger.sh forward <id> --verdict conflict|behind`.** Not person-only: it is mechanical
  routing, called by the babysitter's launcher, the babysit command and the merge action. It accepts phase `pr`
  only and moves the entry to `implement`, unowned, unblocked, attempts reset, writing the brief beside the entry.
  **Git decides, not the caller** (the `deployed` precedent, `ledger-lifecycle.sh:168`): `forward` re-reads
  `pr-watch.sh state` and refuses unless the live verdict equals `--verdict`, so no caller can pull a CLEAN PR
  off a person's `human:merge` gate. In lanes it is an **ask rule**, like `block` (`hefesto-setup.sh:135`): the
  interactive babysit already raises a dialog for `block --kind conflict`; the headless launcher and the merge
  action call it from inside helpers (no tool call, no dialog), which is where the friction HEF-27 measured is.
- **D4 — the brief is generated, not authored.** A fixed template filled with the PR number, URL, head SHA, base
  branch and verdict, copied to `<id>.forward-<n>.md`, sha256 recorded in `.forwards[]`, re-hashed at launch and
  handed to the implement worker as delimited data (the follow-up pattern).
- **D5 — merge, never rebase.** The worker runs `git fetch` + `git merge origin/<base>` in the entry's worktree and
  pushes to the same branch without force; the PR URL stays the same. A force-push or a rebase is a failure.
- **D6 — a loop cap of 3 forwards per PR.** The 4th `forward` on the same PR URL blocks the entry `conflict`
  instead (a person decides); the `conflict` block kind and its form row stay for that case and for entries
  already blocked before this release. The person's way past the cap is `forward … --past-cap --by <name>`: a
  person-only form of the verb (`is_person_sub`, orchestrator lane only, ask rule), which skips the count but
  not the live-verdict check. Bound: ≤ 3 forwards × the implement stall cap (3 attempts) per PR before a person
  is asked.
- **D11 — the worker tests before it commits the merge.** `git merge --no-commit --no-ff origin/<base>`, resolve,
  run the tests, then commit. A red suite after the merge is a semantic conflict of the same nature as a
  two-sided edit, so the worker runs `git merge --abort` (the worktree is back on the PR head, nothing pushed;
  `git reset --hard` is denied by `block-destructive-commands.sh` and is never needed) and stops `human:clarify`
  with the failing output and the files the merge touched — not `failed`, whose stall shows a person only a
  summary.
- **D12 — what `forward` may clear.** Allowed blocks: none, `human:merge` (the gate is re-earned: the entry
  reaches `human:merge` again only after the verifier passes the new head), and `conflict`. Every other block
  (`human:intake`, `human:plan-approval`, `human:clarify`, `human:plan-review`, `ci`, `stall`, `budget`,
  `verdict`) refuses: those are a person's or another gate's to clear (the invariant at `ledger.sh:560-571`).
- **D7 — the two-sided question travels in a new `question` field** (≤ 8000 chars) of the implement worker's
  structured output; the launcher writes it beside the entry and passes it as `block --question`. The 2000-char
  summary is too small for two hunks.
- **D8 — mechanical classes are a closed list** (FR-009). Anything outside the list is two-sided-with-intent.
- **D9 — the test command is the project's own**, as the implement worker already finds it (project CLAUDE.md /
  the `quality-tooling` skill), run through `hooks/lane-build.sh` when the launch prints the lane-cache rule
  (`session-launch.sh:603`). No new config key.
- **D10 — HEF-30 (`merge_by: auto`) is out of scope.** This feature supplies its precondition: an entry reaches
  `human:merge` only from a head the verifier passed, and an entry whose PR cannot be merged forward is blocked
  (`human:clarify` or `conflict`), never `human:merge`.

## User Scenarios

### US1: A PR behind or conflicting with its base goes back to the build stage [P1]
- **Given** an entry in phase `pr` whose PR's `pr-watch.sh state` verdict is `conflict` (DIRTY) or `behind` (BEHIND)
- **When** the deploy stage reads that verdict (headless babysit run, interactive `/hefesto:hef.babysit`, or the lane
  merge's state step / `action stop --block conflict`)
- **Then** `ledger.sh forward` moves the entry to phase `implement`, unowned and unblocked, with a hashed
  merge-forward brief recorded, and `ledger.sh next --stage build` returns it — no form is shown.
- **Edge:** the same PR was already forwarded 3 times → the entry is blocked `conflict` instead and appears in the
  orchestrator's form.
- **Error:** `forward` on an entry not in phase `pr`, with no PR URL, whose live verdict is not the `--verdict`
  given, blocked on a kind D12 does not allow, or with a merge action `approved`/`taken` for it, exits non-zero
  with what it saw and changes nothing (constitution 5).
- **Must NOT:** block the entry `conflict` on a first conflict; leave it in `pr`; call `ledger.sh directive`;
  move a CLEAN PR off `human:merge`.
- Touches: `hooks/pr-watch.sh`, `hooks/ledger.sh`, `hooks/ledger-lifecycle.sh`, `hooks/ledger-recipes.sh`,
  `hooks/session-launch.sh`, `commands/hef.babysit.md`, `commands/hef.orchestrate.md`; tests `tests/smoke.sh`,
  `tests/smoke-merge.sh`, a new `tests/smoke-forward.sh`.

### US2: The build worker merges the base forward and the verifier re-checks [P1]
- **Given** an `implement` entry with an unconsumed merge-forward brief and an existing worktree on the PR branch
- **When** the implement launch runs
- **Then** the worker's prompt carries the brief as data and the merge-forward instruction (fetch the base, merge it
  in, resolve only mechanical conflicts, run the project's tests through `lane-build.sh`, push to the same branch,
  outcome `pr` with the same `pr_url`); on outcome `pr` the brief is marked consumed, the entry advances to
  `verify`, the verifier runs its full gate chain on the new head, and a pass lands the entry in `pr` blocked
  `human:merge` as today.
- **Edge:** the merge is clean (no conflicted file, e.g. BEHIND) → the worker still runs the tests before pushing.
- **Error:** the tests fail after the (uncommitted) merge and the failure is not fixed by one of the mechanical
  classes → `git merge --abort`, nothing committed or pushed, outcome `blocked` `human:clarify` with the failing
  output and the merged files as the `question` (D11). A worker crash is still `failed` (stall cap applies).
- **Must NOT:** re-run spec/plan/tasks; rebase; force-push; open a second PR; advance with an unverified head.
- Touches: `hooks/session-launch.sh` (prompt block, transcription), `hooks/ledger.sh` (`record --forward-consumed`);
  tests `tests/smoke-forward.sh` (fake claude), an eval case.

### US3: A two-sided edit with intent stops as a question [P1]
- **Given** a merge-forward where both sides changed the same lines and the change is not in a mechanical class
- **When** the worker reaches that conflict
- **Then** it aborts the merge (`git merge --abort`), pushes nothing, and stops with outcome `blocked`,
  `blocked_on: human:clarify` and a `question` holding both hunks (path, the PR side, the base side, the merge-base
  text when present); the launcher writes the question beside the entry and blocks with `--question`, and
  `ledger.sh questions <id>` shows it to the orchestrator.
- **Edge:** several two-sided files → one question per file, all in the same `question` text.
- **Error:** the worker reports `human:clarify` with an empty `question` → the launcher blocks with the summary as
  the question (never an empty question file).
- **Must NOT:** pick a side; leave a half-merged worktree; consume the brief (the next run, with the answer,
  resumes the merge-forward).
- Touches: `hooks/session-launch.sh` (schema `question`, transcription, answers block for `implement`).

### US4: The person's answer reaches the next merge-forward run [P2]
- **Given** an entry blocked `human:clarify` by a merge-forward question that the person answered through the
  orchestrator's form (`answer`, existing flow)
- **When** the next implement launch runs
- **Then** the prompt carries both the unconsumed brief and the person's answers as delimited data, and the worker
  merges again, resolving that conflict as answered.
- **Must NOT:** treat the answer text as instructions beyond this item (a tool or setting in it is reported).
- Touches: `hooks/session-launch.sh`.

### US5: Docs and forms describe the new route [P2]
- **Given** the orchestrator's Retry form, the babysit command and the quickstart
- **When** a person reads them
- **Then** they say a conflict or a behind PR goes back to the build stage by itself, and the `conflict` form
  row (only after the cap, or a legacy block) offers **Merge forward** →
  `ledger.sh forward <id> --verdict <live verdict> --past-cap --by "<name>"` · **Later** — instead of a plain
  `unblock` that re-runs the babysitter. A refusal (the live verdict is no longer conflict/behind) is shown to
  the person; then **Retry** (`unblock`) is the right answer and the row offers it.
- Touches: `commands/hef.orchestrate.md`, `commands/hef.babysit.md`, `docs/quickstart.md`,
  `docs/quickstart.pt-BR.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/install.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | `pr-watch.sh state` returns verdict `behind` for an open, non-draft PR with `mergeStateStatus: BEHIND` and passing or absent checks; `conflict` for `DIRTY` is unchanged; `mergeable` covers only `CLEAN` and `HAS_HOOKS`. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | `ledger.sh forward <id> --verdict conflict\|behind` accepts an entry in phase `pr` with a PR URL, and sets `phase = implement`, `owner = null`, `attempts = 0`, `blocked_on = null`, appends `.forwards[] = {n, pr_url, head_sha, base, verdict, sha256, at}` and an event `forward`; it prints one line naming the move. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | `forward` refuses (non-zero exit, message with what it saw, entry byte-identical) when: the entry is not in phase `pr`, has no PR URL, or is terminal; `--verdict` is not `conflict`/`behind`; the live `pr-watch.sh state` verdict differs from `--verdict` (or the read fails); `blocked_on` is a kind other than none, `human:merge`, `conflict` (D12); a merge action for the entry is `approved` or `taken`; or it runs inside a launched worker (`HEFESTO_WORKER`). | P1 | US1 |
| FR-004 | The brief is generated by `forward` from a fixed template with the PR number, URL, head SHA, base branch and verdict, written to `<ledger dir>/<id>.forward-<n>.md` (never through a link), its sha256 stored in the `.forwards[]` record. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-005 | When an entry already has 3 `.forwards[]` records for its current PR URL, `forward` blocks the entry `conflict` instead (phase stays `pr`) and says so; a forward on a new PR URL counts from zero. `--past-cap --by <name>` skips the count (all FR-003 refusals still apply) and records `by` in the forward record and event; it is a person-only form (`is_person_sub` in `hooks/lane-lib.sh`, so lane-guard and `ledger.sh` admit it from the orchestrator lane only). | P1 | US1, US5 |
| FR-006 | The headless deploy run (`session-launch.sh deploy`) routes verdict `conflict` and `behind` to `ledger.sh forward`; the babysit schema's verdict enum includes `behind`. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-007 | The lane merge's state step (`merge_state_step`) and `action stop --block conflict` route `conflict`/`behind` to the `forward` move (the action still stops), instead of `merge_block_conflict` leaving the entry in `pr`. | P1 | US1 |
| FR-008 | `/hefesto:hef.babysit` step 4 runs `ledger.sh forward <id> --verdict <v>` for `conflict` and `behind` (still never a rebase in the babysitter itself). | P1 | US1 |
| FR-009 | The implement launch, for an entry with an unconsumed forward record, verifies the brief's sha256 (mismatch → die, nothing launched) and puts it in the prompt as delimited data with the merge-forward instruction: fetch the base, `git merge --no-commit --no-ff` it (never rebase), commit only after the tests pass (D11), resolve only the mechanical classes — (a) both sides added distinct lines at the same place (keep both, base side first), (b) the conflicting lines are a count, version or generated value the suite computes (take the base side, then regenerate/recompute so the suite agrees), (c) one side's hunk equals the merge-base text (take the other side) — run the project's test command (through `lane-build.sh` when the lane-cache rule is printed), push to the same branch without force, report outcome `pr` with the same `pr_url`. It must not re-spec, re-plan or re-task. | P1 | US2 |
| FR-010 | On implement outcome `pr`, the launcher marks the open forward record consumed (`ledger.sh record <id> --forward-consumed`) before advancing to `verify`; on `blocked human:clarify` or `failed` the record stays open. | P1 | US2 |
| FR-011 | After a forward, the verifier's full gate chain (unchanged) runs against the new head, and only a pass reaches `pr` + `human:merge`; a verdict FAIL blocks `verdict` as today. | P1 | US2 |
| FR-012 | The implement structured-output schema gains an optional `question` string (≤ 8000 chars); on `blocked` with `human:clarify` the launcher writes the question (or, when empty, the summary) to `<ledger dir>/<id>.question-<ts>.md` and blocks with `--question`, so `ledger.sh questions <id>` returns it. | P1 | US3 |
| FR-013 | The merge-forward instruction requires, for any conflict outside the FR-009 classes, `git merge --abort`, no push, outcome `blocked`, `blocked_on: human:clarify`, and a `question` listing per file the path, the PR-side hunk, the base-side hunk and the merge-base text. | P1 | US3 |
| FR-013a | The merge-forward instruction requires, when the tests fail on the uncommitted merge and no mechanical class explains it, `git merge --abort`, no commit, no push, outcome `blocked` `human:clarify`, and a `question` with the failing test output (tail, ≤ 4000 chars) and the files the merge changed (D11). | P1 | US2 |
| FR-014 | The implement launch includes the person's answers (the existing `answers` data block) for an implement-phase entry that has answered questions, alongside the unconsumed brief. | P2 | US4 |
| FR-015 | The orchestrator's `conflict` row reads the live verdict and offers **Merge forward** → `ledger.sh forward <id> --verdict <it> --past-cap --by "<name>"` · **Later**, or, when the verdict is no longer `conflict`/`behind`, **Retry** → `ledger.sh unblock <id>` · **Later**; the deploy-pass text no longer says Retry sends a conflict back to the babysit. | P2 | US5 |
| FR-016 | Docs (`hef.babysit.md`, `hef.orchestrate.md`, quickstart EN + pt-BR, architecture, install) and a `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` entry describe the route; `forward` is listed in `ledger.sh` usage. `hef.babysit.md` step 4 notes that headless the launcher does the forward (a `ledger.sh` refusal inside a worker is expected, as step 5 says for blocks). | P2 | US5 |
| FR-017 | Every new guard has a mutation check in `tests/smoke-forward.sh` (reintroduce the defect, the suite goes red): verdict `behind`; the phase guard; the live-verdict check; the D12 block-kind refusal; the merge-action refusal; the worker refusal; the cap and `--past-cap`'s person-only gate; the brief hash check; the routing of deploy and merge `conflict`/`behind`; the consumed-only-on-`pr` rule; the `--question` transcription. | P1 | all |
| FR-018 | `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` adds `ledger.sh forward` to the lanes' **ask** rules in both spellings (`Bash($h/ledger.sh forward:*)`, `Bash(bash $h/ledger.sh forward:*)`) and to its own rule check, asserted by the setup test. | P2 | US1, US5 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | A fixture entry in `pr` whose fake `gh` reports `BEHIND` goes, through `session-launch.sh deploy` with a fake claude reporting `behind`, to phase `implement` with an open forward record and no block — and with a fake implement worker reporting `pr` on the same URL, then a passing fake verifier, ends in `pr` blocked `human:merge`, the forward record consumed: no form at any step. | `tests/smoke-forward.sh` |
| SC-002 | The same path with a fake worker reporting `blocked human:clarify` + a two-hunk `question` ends blocked `human:clarify` with `ledger.sh questions` printing both hunks and the forward record still open. | `tests/smoke-forward.sh` |
| SC-003 | A 4th forward on the same PR URL blocks `conflict`, and `--past-cap --by p` then forwards it (outside a lane); `forward` on a `verify`-phase entry, on a `human:merge` entry whose live verdict is `mergeable`, on a `human:intake` entry, and under `HEFESTO_WORKER=1` each exits non-zero and leaves the entry byte-identical. | `tests/smoke-forward.sh` |
| SC-004 | Each FR-017 mutation, applied in-test with `sed` to a scratch copy, makes the matching assertion fail (`bad "mutation survived: …"`). | `tests/smoke-forward.sh` |
| SC-005 | Behaviour: given a fixture repo whose PR branch is behind with a one-sided CHANGELOG-list conflict, the worker merges, keeps both entries, pushes the same branch, outcome `pr`; given a true two-sided edit of the same function line, it aborts and returns `human:clarify` with both hunks. | `evals/merge-forward-mechanical`, `evals/merge-forward-two-sided` (`claude plugin eval`, live tier) |
| SC-006 | `tests/smoke.sh` tier 1 passes; no hook exceeds the delta gate. | `bash tests/smoke.sh` |

## Clarifications
_None — every open point was decidable from the code; see Decisions D1–D10._
